title: M/s Natural Water Industries v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sangeeta Chandra, J.; Saurabh Srivastava, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; relegated to Chapter-VI; EE to decide in two weeks.
headnote: Chapter-VI of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the forum for disputed bills and meter-malfunction complaints. A writ seeking mandamus to restore a disconnected commercial connection by deciding a pending representation was disposed of by directing the consumer to apply under that Chapter, with a two-week window for the application and a further two weeks for the Executive Engineer to pass orders.
facts: The petitioner, a small-scale MSME registered on 11 November 2016 for manufacture of refined drinking water, held a commercial connection. It complained on 11 July 2022 that the meter was malfunctioning. A bill of Rs 17,16,178 was then raised and supply was disconnected on 25 July 2022. A representation dated 2 August 2022 to the Executive Engineer, PuVVNL, Ghazipur, remained pending. The writ sought mandamus to restore the connection by deciding that representation.

holding_units.topic: disputed bills and meter malfunction — Chapter-VI forum
holding_units.holding: Disputed electricity bills and complaints of meter malfunction fall under Chapter-VI of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A consumer seeking restoration after disconnection on a disputed bill is to apply to the competent authority under that Chapter; if the application is made within two weeks, the Executive Engineer shall consider it and pass appropriate orders within a further two weeks. The writ was disposed of on that direction without a merits grant or refusal.
holding_units.flag: Court invoked Chapter-VI generally for disputed bills and meter malfunction without identifying a specific clause (e.g. 6.5 or 6.8).

principle_tags.application: The Division Bench treated Chapter-VI as the pathway for the consumer's disputed-bill and meter complaint and refused a restoration mandamus on a pending representation, directing a time-bound Chapter-VI application to the Executive Engineer instead.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the Rs 17,16,178 bill, alleged meter malfunction, legality of the 25 July 2022 disconnection, and entitlement to restoration
not_decided.note: Writ disposed without examining the merits; consumer directed to apply under Chapter-VI.
